# Limits: approaching a value

This reviewed teaching adaptation covers the first limit example on PDF page 14 (printed page 8) of the UNISA guide. It is a small pilot, not a replacement for the full unit.

A left-hand limit describes the value approached from smaller inputs. A right-hand limit describes the value approached from larger inputs. A two-sided limit exists when both approaches agree.

Consider

$$
f(x)=\frac{x^2-4}{x-2}.
$$

At $x=2$, the denominator is zero, so $f(2)$ is undefined. For $x\ne2$, factor and cancel:

$$
\frac{x^2-4}{x-2}=\frac{(x-2)(x+2)}{x-2}=x+2.
$$

From either side of 2, the function values approach 4:

$$
\lim_{x\to 2}\frac{x^2-4}{x-2}=4.
$$

The value of a limit can exist even when the function is undefined at the point. Move the slider towards 2 from each side and compare the approaching values. At exactly 2 the graph has a hole.

blocks.title: Approach a hole. Discover the limit.
blocks.caption: For x different from 2, (x²−4)/(x−2) equals x+2. Both sides approach 4, although the value at 2 is undefined. This widget adapts the guide’s numerical tables.
